entities.summary: Munio of Zamora, O.P., was a Spanish Dominican friar who became the seventh Master General of the Dominican Order in 1285, and later a bishop. He played a crucial role in the spread of Dominican spirituality and education throughout Southern Europe during the Late Medieval period. Munio's contributions to the Dominican Order's influence can be seen in the establishment of numerous monasteries and schools across the region. His tenure as Master General marked a significant turning point in the Order's development, as he worked to consolidate its authority and promote its mission. Munio's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his efforts helped shape the Dominican Order into the powerful and respected institution it remains today. The Dominican Order's influence can still be felt in the many universities, monasteries, and churches that dot the landscape of Southern Europe, a testament to Munio's enduring impact on the region's spiritual and cultural heritage.
